B. Is this measure already running in Southwest Finland wellbeing services county (or in the Tyks university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure reduce deaths among the people it reaches, and by how much?
Measure: Smoking cessation started at the first specialist visit. Every current smoker with suspected lung cancer gets cessation medication and counselling at the first visit, as part of preparing for curative treatment.
supported_en: Quitting after diagnosis was linked to 33% lower all-cause mortality (hazard ratio 0.67, range 0.53–0.85) in early-stage non-small-cell lung cancer (Annals of Internal Medicine, 2021).
not_supported_en: The study does not show the effect of offering treatment, only of actually quitting, and it reports no quit rate after an offer.
in_use_quote: Apua tupakoinnin lopettamiseen saat Tyksin keuhkosairauksien poliklinikan tupakastavieroitushoitajalta, puh. 010 853 3324.
missing_en: No page shows that every smoker with suspected lung cancer is routinely offered cessation medicine and counselling at the first visit.
summary_en: Tyks's quit-smoking page says patients can get help from a cessation nurse at the lung clinic, which is where all lung cancer diagnosis in the area is done; no page says every smoker with suspected lung cancer is given medicine and counselling at the first visit. A Moscow cohort study of 517 smokers with early-stage non-small-cell lung cancer (Annals of Internal Medicine, 2021) found 33% lower all-cause mortality in those who quit after diagnosis (hazard ratio 0.67, range 0.53–0.85). That compares quitters with people who kept smoking, not people offered treatment with people who were not, so the effect across everyone reached will be smaller.
unanswered_en: No page was found showing whether Tyks refers smokers with suspected lung cancer to its cessation nurse routinely at the first visit.
